subject: Approach to cross-validate a mirt model

messages.author: a29b76a7fee2ac43
messages.subject: Approach to cross-validate a mirt model
parts:
Hello,

I am using the following approach for a cross-validation test (and check the prediction) for my mirt model and wonder if someone who has experience in performing similar tests can comment on whether it is valid:

1) The mirt model MIRT_A was constructed based on Data_A.
2) The cross-validated dataset is called Data_B. A separate mirt model MIRT_B (with the same expression/factor structure as MIRT_A) was constructed based on Data_B.
3) I generate fscores(MIRT_A) using the response.pattern of Data_B.
4) I generate fscores(MIRT_B)
5) Both 3 and 4 had the same number of rows (same participants now),
6) Next, I calculate the RMSE ability score differences between 3 and 4 (square root of the mean differences between each ability).
7) If RMSE is low, say <=0.5, then it is considered acceptable prediction model?

What do you think?

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: Approach to cross-validate a mirt model
parts:
I think the approach is close, but it's generally not my favorite as the trait estimates are commingled with the response vectors themselves. More ideal would be to compare the models based on the marginal likelihood to remove any effect of the point estimates, but I'm not entirely sure the best way of going about this. I'll put the idea on my radar, though if you know of a citation to help out with this then I'm all ears.

Phil
